newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT MARKETS OUTLOOK - Quiet ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT MARKETS OUTLOOK - Quiet ahead of holiday.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries look to take a pause Friday, as the market prepares for a long-holiday weekend following another week of rallying.
With Veterans Day shutting the market on Monday, and giving the market at 1400 EST/1900 GMT close Friday, market participants expect a very quiet day, with little activity.
"My guess is that we're kind of going to hang here," said Stephen Slifer, chief economist at Lehman Brothers Inc. "We'll either stay here or back up slightly."
After falling nearly a point early Thursday, bonds did an about face and ended the New York session up one point.
The yield fell to an eight-month low of 6.53 percent.

With no key economic data until next week, players don't see a reason to sell, or even take profits for that matter. "People are just staying long," said a trader at a primary dealer. "People think the market will keep going higher. Some guys are short, but until the last guy is short we ain't going anywhere."
If projections hold true, it would be the second straight week the market would end on an up note -- and that's after a week with a lot of new supply.
